HUMARI KAHANI · OUR STORY

A small town. A big dream.

Every evening, in the narrow lanes of a small town, a boy watched food being made with love — and served without care. Oil reused till it smoked, water nobody trusted, hands nobody had ever seen. He loved those flavours. He never stopped wishing he could trust those kitchens.

So he made a promise — one day, he would serve the same street food. The chole, the samose, the dahi vade. But clean. Honest. Made the way you would for your own ghar. That boy grew up, and the promise grew into The Dream Food.

“Main sirf khana nahi, bharosa serve karna chahta hoon — swaad aisa, ghar jaisa, aur safai jaisi sapno mein hoti hai.”

— RRITU RAJ, FOUNDER

GHAR PAR BANAO · MASTERCLASS

Delhi Chole Bhature — the real
recipe.

The exact street-style method we'll serve at The Dream Food — tea-dark chole, pillowy bhature. Make it at home, taste the dream early.

Haath se gunda masala, dil se banaya.

✧ Chef's Tips

  • Curd at room temperature + a pinch of soda = extra-fluffy bhature.
  • Never skip the tea-water chole trick — it is the Dilli secret.
  • Chole tastes deeper the next day; make it a few hours ahead.

FOR THE CHOLE

FOR THE BHATURE

The Method

01Soak the chana overnight with tea leaves tied in muslin — this gives Delhi's signature dark, rich colour.
02Pressure-cook the chana with the tea bag until butter-soft. Reserve the cooking liquor.
03Heat desi ghee. Add whole spices, onions and ginger-garlic paste. Cook until deeply golden.
04Add tomato puree, chole masala and anardana. Cook until the masala releases its ghee.
05Add chana and reserved liquor. Simmer gently until thick, dark and full of flavour.
06Knead bhatura dough with maida, sooji, curd and soda. Rest, roll and fry until beautifully puffed.
